questions.question: What does the voltage of a battery measure?
options: The resistance offered to the flowing current
The strength with which it can 'push' current around a circuit
The total number of electrons stored inside the battery
The rate at which electrons are destroyed in the circuit

questions.question: In a series circuit, how does the voltage across each individual component relate to the total voltage of the battery?
options: The voltage across each component adds up to the total voltage of the battery
The voltage across each component is always equal to the total voltage of the battery
The voltage across each component is subtracted from the battery's voltage to find the remaining current
The voltage across each component is multiplied together to equal the battery's voltage

questions.question: If three cells, each of 1.5 V, are connected in series to make a battery, what is the total voltage of this battery?
In which direction does a battery push electric charge (electrons) around a complete circuit?
options: In both directions at the same time, alternating rapidly
One way round the complete circuit
From the outer surface of the wires to the center
From the light bulb towards both terminals simultaneously

questions.question: Which of the following is true about electric charges in a circuit's wires when the circuit is turned off?
options: There are no electric charges in the wires at all
Electric charges are only present in the battery, not in the wires
Electric charges exist in all atoms of the wires and components, even when turned off
The charges are completely destroyed and must be recreated by the battery

questions.question: What happens to the electrons throughout a circuit at the moment it is switched on?
options: Electrons only start moving near the positive terminal first
Electrons everywhere in the circuit start moving at the same time
Electrons slowly travel one by one from the battery through the wires
Electrons at the negative terminal move, while others wait for them to collide

questions.question: How fast do individual electrons actually drift through a circuit when current is flowing?
options: At the speed of light
At a speed of several meters per second
At a slow speed of just a few millimeters each second
At a speed of about 100 kilometers per hour

questions.question: Why can current not flow through a faulty filament bulb?
options: The glass bulb has become too hot to conduct electricity
The filament is broken, preventing the current from flowing through it
The metal base of the bulb has turned into an insulator
The bulb's filament has absorbed all the electrons

questions.question: Under what condition is an electric circuit considered incomplete?
options: If there are any gaps in the circuit, including those hidden in faulty wires or components
Only if the battery is completely disconnected and removed from the room
If the wires are drawn using a ruler in a diagram
If the circuit contains more than two light bulbs

questions.question: How can a circuit with a single faulty component be made to work again?
options: By increasing the voltage of the battery to melt the component
By turning the battery around so the current flows backwards
By using a wire to bypass the faulty component
By adding another faulty component in series with the first one

questions.question: What is a series circuit?
options: A circuit with multiple branching loops for current to split into
An electric circuit with one complete loop from one end of a battery to the other
A circuit that can only function using static electricity
A circuit where components are connected to different batteries

questions.question: How does an ammeter affect the current in the circuit it is measuring?
options: It significantly reduces the current to protect the battery
It doubles the current to make the measurement easier
It measures the current flowing through it without affecting the current in the circuit
It stops the current completely while taking a reading

questions.question: Which of the following describes the current at different points in a series circuit?
options: The current is highest near the positive terminal of the battery
The current is the same everywhere in a series circuit
The current decreases after passing through each light bulb
The current is lowest near the negative terminal of the battery

questions.question: What happens to the current in a series circuit when you add an extra bulb to it?
options: The current changes everywhere in the circuit, on both sides of the new component
The current only decreases on the side of the circuit after the new bulb
The current only decreases on the side of the circuit before the new bulb
The current remains completely unchanged everywhere

questions.question: How must a voltmeter be connected to measure the voltage across a component?
options: It must be connected in series, in the middle of a single cut wire
It must be connected across the terminals of the component
It must be connected directly between the positive terminal of the battery and the earth
It must be wrapped around the plastic insulation of the wire

questions.question: Why are metals difficult to charge by rubbing?
options: Because they do not contain any electrons or protons
Because electric charge flows easily through them, preventing charge from building up
Because rubbing them destroys the atoms on their surface
Because they are highly magnetic, which cancels out electrostatic charge
